title: New Phishing Platforms Bypass Microsoft 365 MFA Using Device Code Attacks
excerpt: Subscription-based phishing kits Forg365 and Kali365, sold on Telegram for as little as $250 a month, are enabling even low-skill attackers to hijack corporate Microsoft 365 accounts by abusing legitimate authentication flows.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Forg365 combines device code phishing and AI tactics, bypassing Microsoft 365 MFA for $400 monthly.
  • Kali365, a similar platform, has been linked to hundreds of attacks since its detection in April 2026.
  • A misconfigured server exposed a year-long phishing campaign, compromising 218 corporate victims across 12 countries.
  • Experts urge disabling device code authentication and auditing mailbox rules to enhance security against these attacks.

A new generation of phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platforms is turning Microsoft 365's own authentication infrastructure against its users, rendering traditional multi-factor authentication protections largely ineffective.

Security researchers at ZeroBEC this month disclosed Forg365, a subscription-based phishing platform distributed via Telegram that combines device code phishing, adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) session theft, and AI-assisted lure creation into a single operator dashboard. The platform costs $400 per month or $3,800 annually and includes a five-day free trial.

How the Attack Works

The core technique exploits Microsoft's legitimate device code authentication flow — the same process users encounter when signing into streaming services on smart TVs. Attackers send phishing emails impersonating trusted services such as DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign, or SharePoint. The messages direct victims to Microsoft's real verification page and instruct them to enter a code.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Y1jPDDk8z3Q

Once the victim completes the process, the attacker captures OAuth access and refresh tokens, granting persistent access to Outlook, Teams, and OneDrive — without ever needing a password or triggering additional MFA challenges.

> **"The FBI issued a public service announcement on May 21 warning about Kali365, a similar PhaaS platform first spotted in April 2026 and also distributed through Telegram."**

Forg365's operator panel includes account management, OAuth app configuration, SMTP rotation, AI email generation, token vaulting, and keyword alerts. The platform also offers ForgCookie, a Chromium browser extension that automatically refreshes Microsoft single sign-on cookies, converting a one-time phishing success into prolonged account access.

FBI Sounds the Alarm on Kali365

Forg365 is not operating in isolation. The FBI issued a public service announcement on May 21 warning about Kali365, a similar PhaaS platform first spotted in April 2026 and also distributed through Telegram. Available for as little as $250 per month, Kali365 provides AI-generated phishing lures, automated campaign templates, real-time victim tracking dashboards, and OAuth token capture capabilities.

"The FBI issued a public service announcement on May 21 warning about Kali365, a similar PhaaS platform first spotted in April 2026 and also distributed through Telegram."

"Kali365 lowers the barrier of entry," the FBI stated, noting that attackers can access Microsoft 365 services "without needing a password or completing any additional MFA challenges." Security researchers documented hundreds of Kali365 attacks in April alone.

Arctic Wolf researchers noted the platform supports lateral phishing — using compromised accounts to send phishing emails to the victim's own contacts, rapidly expanding the attack surface.

Year-Long Campaign Exposed by Misconfigured Server

The industrialisation of these attacks was further underscored by research from French security firm Lexfo, which discovered a misconfigured server in Budapest exposing the complete toolkit of three phishing operators using Evilginx-based AitM platforms against corporate Microsoft 365 accounts.

The most prolific operator, tracked as saroula01, had run a device code phishing campaign undetected since June 2025, accumulating 218 confirmed victims across 12 countries. Roughly 94 percent were corporate targets. Captured tokens had been silently refreshed up to 25 times, maintaining persistent access long after the initial compromise.

All three operators used generative AI to build their tooling, with AI co-author metadata visible in code commits. Lexfo concluded that "the barrier to running a functional AiTM campaign has dropped close to zero."

"The victim sees real Microsoft authentication surfaces, but the code authorizes an attacker-controlled session."

— ZeroBEC, email security researchers

What Enterprises Should Do

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) recommends blocking device code authentication unless there is a specific business need. Security teams should review mailbox artifacts after device code events, audit mail-flow rules for unauthorised changes, and decommission legacy email aliases.

For Indian IT services firms and diaspora professionals managing global enterprise environments, the threat is acute. Microsoft 365 is the dominant productivity platform across corporate India and the multinational clients that Indian IT companies serve. A single compromised account can provide attackers with access to sensitive business documents, client communications, and internal systems through single sign-on.

Organisations should also monitor for suspicious device registrations — Forg365 campaigns have registered devices with names prefixed with "Forg365-," providing a useful detection marker.
